land.text: the German Reich of the Weimar Republic

predecessors.note: Same state, new regime: Hitler became Chancellor on 30 January 1933 and the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933 completed the change; the two dossiers meet in March 1933.

successors.note: 1945-1949 Allied occupation zones (no Cliopatria row): Potsdam Agreement of 2 August 1945.

land.text: German land east of the Oder-Neisse line, per the Potsdam Agreement

successors.note: Poland and the Soviet Union took the lands east of the Oder-Neisse line.
Austria is also a Cliopatria successor entity.

capitals.name: Berlin
capitals.note: Infobox capital Berlin; the Flensburg Government of Karl Donitz was arrested on 23 May 1945 (infobox).

rulers.name: Adolf Hitler
rulers.title: Fuhrer; Chancellor since 1933
rulers.note: Infobox: head of state 1934-1945 and Chancellor 1933-1945.

correction.text: Germany 1933-1934 without the Saar; the Saar is added by the 1935 gain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Nazi row starts in 1936, but the state is founded in March 1933, at the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933 (infobox); 30 January 1933 is the seizure of power. Cliopatria's Weimar 1932 shape already contains the Saar (it grows by 16 cells at the Saar in 1932), yet the Saar returned only in 1935 (Territorial evolution page), so it is cut out until the 1935 gain.

498 k km2 (infobox gives 633,786 km2 for 1939 only, so no direct check). Germany with the Saar (returned 1935) and East Prussia; the 7 March 1936 Rhineland remilitarisation (Nazi Germany page) moved no border.

626,625 km2 against the infobox's 633,786 km2 for 1939 (ratio 0.99): Germany plus Austria (12/13 March) and the Sudetenland (1-10 October). The shape is the end-of-1938 state; the ledger dates the two gains.

correction.text: the Reich of 1938 plus Memel and Danzig, without the Protectorate and Slovakia; the October 1939 Polish annexations are added by the ledger gain

keyframe_review.note: 699,301 km2 against the infobox's 633,786 km2 (ratio 1.10). The shape folds in Bohemia and Moravia (Protectorate, 15-16 March) and part of Slovakia, which the pages treat as occupied and puppet land, not Reich land. Memel (23 March) stays in.

correction.text: the Reich of 1939 plus the annexed Polish lands, Eupen-Malmedy and Alsace-Lorraine; Denmark, Norway, the Low Countries, northern France, the General Government and the Protectorate are occupation, not Reich land

keyframe_review.note: 1,637,988 km2 against the infobox's 823,505 km2 for 1940 (ratio 1.99): Cliopatria draws the Reich plus Poland, Denmark, Norway, the Low Countries and northern France as one state. The German-occupied Europe table separates annexed land from occupation; the occupied lands are carried as occupation events.

correction.text: the Reich of 1940 plus northern Slovenia and the Bialystok region; the Balkan lands are occupation; Libya removed (Italian territory throughout the North African campaign page)

keyframe_review.note: 1,880,563 km2. Adds Serbia, Slovenia, Greece (occupied from 6 April 1941) and 255 Libyan cells at about 30 N, which no page supports as German land. The Bialystok region joined East Prussia and northern Slovenia was annexed. North African campaign: Libya is 'Italian territory throughout' (infobox 'Italian Libya placed under British and French military administration'), the Afrika Korps arrived 'in Tripoli in February' 1941 to support Italian units, and the page says nothing of a German annexation or occupation of Libya, so the Libyan cells stay removed.

correction.text: the Reich with Luxembourg (annexed August 1942); the occupied Soviet lands, Serbia and Greece are occupation; Libya is Italian land, not Reich land

keyframe_review.note: 3,035,422 km2. Adds the Baltic states, Belarus, Ukraine and western Russia, all occupation (22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945), and still 164 Libyan cells. Luxembourg is formally annexed in August 1942. North African campaign: Libya is 'Italian territory throughout' (infobox 'Italian Libya placed under British and French military administration'), the Afrika Korps arrived 'in Tripoli in February' 1941 to support Italian units, and the page says nothing of a German annexation or occupation of Libya, so the Libyan cells stay removed.

correction.text: the Reich proper as in 1942; the Soviet lands, France, Tunisia and the Balkans are occupation

keyframe_review.note: 3,309,320 km2, the maximum. The shape now includes Italy-controlled Tunisia cells (75) and 37 Libyan cells and, in 1943, the whole of France; none of these is Reich land. The Tunisian cells are carried by the Tunisia occupation event (November 1942 to 13 May 1943, North African campaign); the Libyan cells are Italian land as above.

correction.text: the Reich at the start of 1944, annexed lands included; the Bialystok district (July), Eupen-Malmedy (September) and Alsace-Lorraine (November) are lost during the year and Luxembourg stays to February 1945 (ledger losses); the Eastern Front page dates the retreat but gives no yearly line for the annexed Polish lands

keyframe_review.note: 2,710,534 km2: the shape loses Ukraine and Russia but gains northern Italy (occupied from 8 September 1943) and Hungary (19 March 1944) and all of Slovakia, none of which is Reich land. The front reached the 1939 Polish-Soviet border on 3 January 1944 (Eastern Front page). This keyframe is the shape at 1 January 1944; the three dated losses of 1944 are ledger events, and the 1945 keyframe drops them.

union.text: the Reich of 1938 plus Memel and Danzig, without the Protectorate and Slovakia; the October 1939 Polish annexations are added by the ledger gain
the annexed lands: Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia, the Ciechanow and Katowice districts; drawn from voivodeships and a radius, approximate
northern Slovenia: Lower Styria and the parts attached to Karnten, approximate

correction.text: the Reich at 1 January 1945: the 1939 Reich with the annexed Polish lands, Memel, Danzig, Luxembourg and northern Slovenia; the Bialystok district, Eupen-Malmedy and Alsace-Lorraine are already gone (lost July, September and November 1944), and the ledger removes Luxembourg (February), Memel, Wartheland and Katowice (January), Danzig-West Prussia and Danzig (March), the Sudetenland and Lower Styria (May)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends in 1944, the Reich in May 1945. The shape is the Reich at 1 January 1945, which differs from the 1944 keyframe by the Bialystok district, Eupen-Malmedy and Alsace-Lorraine (ledger losses of 1944). Soviet forces entered Germany on 13 January 1945 (East Prussian offensive) and the Western Allies crossed the Rhine in March; the dated losses of the annexed lands are ledger events (Memel 28 January, Katowice 27 January, Lodz 19 January, Danzig 30 March), with the contests carrying the pre-1938 eastern lands.

region.text: Germany as the Weimar Republic left it, without the Saar

ledger.note: 1933: the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933 (Nazi Germany infobox: 'Enabling Act: 23 March 1933') ends the Weimar Republic in law, and weimar-republic dissolves into this state in March 1933 (its lead gives 'from 9 November 1918 to 23 March 1933'); the Nazi seizure of power began on 30 January 1933 ('Seizure of power: 30 January 1933'). The page names Germany, not a boundary; the core is the Weimar Republic's land without the Saar, which the League of Nations still administered.

region.text: the Saar, under League of Nations control for fifteen years

ledger.note: 1935: the Saar returns to Germany. Plebiscite 13 January 1935 (90.3 per cent for joining Germany), League Council approval 17 January, German takeover 1 March 1935 (Territorial evolution page); the Nazi Germany page: Germany 'regained control of the Saarland through a referendum held in 1935'.
1938: the Anschluss. Infobox dates the annexation of Austria 12/13 March 1938; after the 11 March ultimatum 'German troops entered Austria the next day'.

region.text: the Sudetenland, the only land the Nazi Germany page names for the Munich settlement

ledger.note: 1938: the Sudetenland passes to Germany. The Munich Agreement was signed 29 September; Hitler 'annexed the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia on 1 October' and the occupation 'would be completed by 10 October' (Territorial evolution page: transfer began 10 October).

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia, the Czech lands outside the Sudetenland

ledger.note: 1939: German troops enter the Czech lands. 'On the morning of 15 March, German troops entered the remaining Czech parts of Czechoslovakia'; Hitler proclaimed the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia on 16 March 1939 'from Prague Castle'. The occupied state is the rump Czecho-Slovakia (counterpart czechoslovakia); the Protectorate was a German creation and has no standing of its own. The page does not say Bohemia and Moravia were annexed directly: drawn as occupation, not Reich land.

region.text: Slovakia, the Slovak Republic (puppet state, 'German Zone of Protection')

ledger.note: 1939: Slovakia becomes a German client state. Slovak Diet declared independence on 14 March 1939 (German occupation of Czechoslovakia page); Slovak Republic listed as a puppet state 23 March 1939 to May 1945 with a German Zone of Protection (German-occupied Europe table). Not annexed.
1939: Lithuania cedes Memel under threat of invasion by sea; the cession treaty was signed 23 March 1939 (Territorial evolution page; the Nazi Germany page: 'in March 1939').
1939: Germany invades Poland on 1 September 1939 ('Invaded 1 Sep 1939; occupied 1 Sep 1939 - 9 May 1945').
1939: Germany 'captured the Free City of Danzig on 1 September 1939'; annexed as Reichsgau Danzig-West Prussia (German-occupied Europe table).

region.text: the annexed lands: Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia, the Ciechanow and Katowice districts; drawn from voivodeships and a radius, approximate

ledger.note: 1939: Poland partitioned. 'Two decrees by Adolf Hitler (8 October and 12 October 1939)' created Reichsgau Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia, the Ciechanow district and the Katowice district; the page names no boundaries.
1939: the Polish campaign ends. 'On 6 October, following the Polish defeat at the Battle of Kock, German and Soviet forces gained full control over Poland' (Invasion of Poland).

region.text: the part of Poland neither annexed nor already German: the General Government, approximate

ledger.note: 1939: the General Government. 'A Fuhrer's decree of October 12, 1939 established the General Government; the decree came into force on October 26, 1939' (the 8 October decree announced the annexation of the western lands). The page names no boundary: the region is the part of Poland neither annexed nor already German, approximate.

1940: Alsace-Lorraine annexed. 'After the invasion of France in 1940, Germany annexed the' region and placed it under adjacent Gaue; the page adds that no formal annexation was declared and gives no month.
1940: Denmark occupied. 'Occupied 9 Apr 1940 - 5 May 1945' as a protectorate state with no annexation; the Nazi Germany page: Denmark 'fell after less than a day'.
1940: Germany invades Norway on 9 April 1940 (German-occupied Europe table; Nazi Germany page: the invasion 'began on 9 April').
1940: the Netherlands occupied from 10 May 1940 under the Reichskommissariat Niederlande; no annexation (table gives the end as 20 May 1945).
1940: Belgium occupied from 10 May 1940; parts annexed (Gau Cologne-Aachen, Reichsgau Wallonien, Reichsgau Flandern). Table gives the end as 4 February 1945.
1940: Luxembourg occupied on 10 May 1940 (annexed as Gau Moselland, see 1942).
1940: the attack in the west begins on 10 May 1940 against France and the Low Countries ('Occupied 10 May 1940'; the Nazi Germany page: Hitler ordered the attack in May 1940).

region.text: Eupen-Malmedy, the Belgian districts taken from Germany in 1919/1920, approximate

ledger.note: 1940: Eupen-Malmedy annexed. 'On 18 May, Eupen-Malmedy was re-integrated into Germany while the rest of the country remained under military occupation' (Eupen-Malmedy; Territorial evolution lists Gau Cologne-Aachen). The region is a radius around the districts, approximate.
1940: Norway 'was fully occupied by early June'.
1940: Norway under the Reichskommissariat Norwegen with a Norway National Government as puppet; occupied until 8 May 1945, never annexed.
1940: France 'surrendered on 22 June'.

region.text: occupied France north of the demarcation line and the Atlantic coast, from Cliopatria's 1940 shape

ledger.note: 1940: the northern and Atlantic zone of France is occupied (table: 'Occupied 10 May 1940'); Vichy France is the French State. Drawn from Cliopatria's 1940 shape cut to France.

region.text: Guernsey, the Bailiwick including Alderney and Sark

ledger.note: 1940: Guernsey. German-occupied Europe table: '30 Jun 1940 - 9 May 1945 (Guernsey)', part of the Military Administration in France.
1940: Jersey. German-occupied Europe table: '1 Jul 1940 - 9 May 1945 (Jersey)'.

region.text: Serbia (Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia)

ledger.note: 1941: Yugoslavia invaded 6 April 1941; the Serbian Military Administration ran 30 April 1941 to January 1945 under a Commissioner Government. Occupied, not annexed.

region.text: northern Slovenia: Lower Styria and the parts attached to Karnten, approximate

ledger.note: 1941: 'Northern Yugoslavia was annexed in April 1941' (Nazi Germany page); Reichsgau Karnten and Steiermark (German-occupied Europe table); the Territorial evolution page names Lower Styria without a date. The region is drawn from Cliopatria's 1941 shape cut to Slovenia.

1941: 'It was established in parts of occupied Yugoslavia on 10 April 1941' and was 'a puppet state of Nazi Germany from 1941 to 1945' (also a protectorate of Fascist Italy 1941-1943 and, from 18 May 1941 to September 1943, 'a territorial condominium of Germany and Italy'). A client, not Reich land.
1941: Greece occupied from 6 April 1941 under a Military Administration with the Hellenic State as puppet; no annexation. Drawn from Cliopatria's 1941 shape cut to Greece.

region.text: the Baltic states, Belarus, Ukraine and western Russia, from Cliopatria's 1942 shape

ledger.note: 1941: Operation Barbarossa 'began just before dawn on 22 June 1941'.

region.text: occupied western and southern Russia without the Crimea, from Cliopatria's 1942 shape

ledger.note: 1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union, 22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariats Ostland and Ukraine. Cliopatria's 1941 shape does not yet include these lands. Part: Russia (the RSFSR dossier dates its first losses to July 1941).

region.text: occupied Ukraine (Reichskommissariat Ukraine), from Cliopatria's 1942 shape

ledger.note: 1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union, 22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariats Ostland and Ukraine. Cliopatria's 1941 shape does not yet include these lands. Part: Ukraine.

1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union, 22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariat Ostland. Cliopatria's 1941 shape does not yet include these lands. Part: Belarus. Moldova, which Cliopatria's shape also holds, is a separate event.

1941: Moldova inside Cliopatria's 1942 shape. The German-occupied Europe table lists only 'parts of the Soviet Union' (22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945) and does not name Moldova; the Moldavian SSR dossier records Romanian, not German, occupation, so this event is a bridge over a silence and the land may belong to kingdom-of-romania instead.

region.text: occupied Lithuania without the Memel district (Reich land from March 1939), from Cliopatria's 1942 shape

ledger.note: 1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union, 22 June 1941 to 10 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariat Ostland. Cliopatria's 1941 shape does not yet include these lands. Part: Lithuania; the Memel district is Reich land (ledger gain of March 1939).

1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union from 22 June 1941 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariat Ostland. Part: Latvia (the Latvian SSR dossier dates the entry of Riga to 1 July 1941).
1941: occupation of parts of the Soviet Union from 22 June 1941 (German-occupied Europe table); Reichskommissariat Ostland. Part: Estonia (the Estonian SSR dossier dates the arrival to July 1941).

1941: Bezirk Bialystok. 'Bialystok District was established on 1 August 1941' (Bezirk Bialystok), attached to East Prussia after the attack on the Soviet Union of June 1941 (Territorial evolution page: attached, not incorporated). The land had been Polish and was part of the Byelorussian SSR from November 1939. Region: the Podlachian voivodeship, approximate.

region.text: the Crimean peninsula, then part of the Russian SFSR

ledger.note: 1941: the Crimea. 'By 16 November, the Wehrmacht had cleared the region' and the fall of Kerch on 16 November left only Sevastopol in Soviet hands; Sevastopol itself surrendered on 4 July 1942 (Siege of Sevastopol).
1941: 6 December, the German attack on Moscow is suspended and the Soviet counteroffensive begins (furthest advance 27 November, Khimki within 30 km of the Kremlin).

region.text: southern Russia: the Don, the Volga at Stalingrad and the Caucasus approaches

ledger.note: 1942: Case Blue launched 28 June; German troops reach the Volga at Stalingrad 23 August; Operation Uranus encircles the 6th Army 19-23 November.
1942: Luxembourg's military occupation ends in annexation: 'formally annexed to Germany in August 1942' (Territorial evolution page).
1942: Luxembourg 'formally annexed to Germany in August 1942' (Gau Moselland).

region.text: the former free zone of France, from the growth of Cliopatria's shape

ledger.note: 1942: Case Anton, the German occupation of the Vichy 'zone libre'. 'By the evening of 10 November 1942, Wehrmacht and Royal Italian Army forces had completed their preparations' and the occupation began on 11 November, after 'the Allied landings in French North Africa on 8 November 1942'. The page gives no end date for it ('liberation of the country in 1944'). The region is the growth of Cliopatria's shape in 1943.

1942: Tunisia. After Operation Torch, 'the Germans and Italians initiated a buildup of troops in Tunisia to fill the vacuum left by Vichy troops' from early November 1942 (North African campaign); french-africa dates the occupation to November 1942.

1943: the Red Army retakes the Russian lands: Orel is retaken on 5 August 1943 and Army Group South withdraws across the Dnieper in September; the page dates none of the other Russian recaptures (the Leningrad and Pskov regions were cleared later). The Crimea has its own end in May 1944.
1943: the 90,000 surviving men of the 6th Army surrender at Stalingrad on 31 January 1943 (the page gives 31 January, not February).
1943: 'The Axis forces surrendered on 13 May 1943 yielding over 275,000 prisoners of war' (North African campaign).

region.text: northern and central Italy outside the two Operational Zones, from Cliopatria's 1944 shape cut to Italy

ledger.note: 1943: German occupation of Italian territory from 8 September 1943 to 2 May 1945, with the Italian Social Republic (German-occupied Europe table); the Allied invasion of Italy is dated 3 September 1943. Not annexed. Whether this land is an occupation or a client (vassal) of the Italian Social Republic is to be settled with eu-21-x. The two Operational Zones are a separate event.

region.text: the Operational Zones of the Adriatic Littoral (Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pola, Fiume, Ljubljana) and the Alpine Foothills (Belluno, South Tyrol, Trentino), modern equivalents, approximate

ledger.note: 1943: 'OZAK was established, with its headquarters in Trieste, on 10 September 1943, by Adolf Hitler', comprising 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)'; the sister zone of the Alpine Foothills (Belluno, South Tyrol, Trentino) 'was established on the same day'. The page calls OZAK 'semi-annexed', 'not incorporated in the German Reich outright, but attached to the Gau of Carinthia', and says both zones were separate from the Italian Social Republic. Drawn as occupation, not Reich land. Pordenone is added because the 1943 province of Udine included it; Ljubljana is a 40 km radius.
1943: Albania. German-occupied Europe table: 'Albanian Kingdom ... 8 Sep 1943 - 29 Nov 1944'.
1943: Monaco. German-occupied Europe table: 'Monaco ... 8 Sep 1943 - 3 Sep 1944'.
1944: Hungary occupied from 19 March 1944 (Government of National Unity), to May 1945; no annexation.

1944: the Crimea retaken. 'An assault across the Perekop Isthmus was launched on 8 April', Sevastopol 'fell on 9 May' and 'the last Axis pockets in the Crimea were destroyed on 12 May' (Crimean offensive).

1944: Ukraine retaken. 'In 1943 and 1944, the Red Army liberated most of territory of the Reichskommissariat in its advance westwards' and 'On 28 July 1944, the Red Army occupied the last part of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in Brest' (Reichskommissariat Ukraine; dissolved 10 November 1944). The ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier ends its occupation in October 1944, counting Transcarpathia, which this event does not.

1944: the Bialystok district goes. 'In July and August 1944, the territory of Bialystok District was taken over by the Red Army up to the Narew-Bobr line' and 'In January 1945, the Red Army overran the last areas' (Bezirk Bialystok).

1944: Operation Bagration, 'fought between 22 June and 19 August 1944', retook Belarus (infobox: 'Red Army retakes all of Byelorussian SSR'); Minsk was liberated on 4 July, Brest on 28 July. The month is the operation's end; the Byelorussian SSR dossier gives 1944 only.

1944: the Second Jassy-Kishinev offensive ran 20 to 29 August 1944 and ended in a Soviet victory over German and Romanian forces; the page does not describe the area retaken, so the end of the Moldova bridge is confidence 1.

1944: liberation of France (the zone occupied in 1940). 'On 25 August 1944 Paris was liberated' and Operation Dragoon began 15 August (Liberation of France); the page's infobox runs the liberation '6 June 1944 - 8 May 1945', with the Atlantic pockets held to 8 May 1945 and Alsace-Lorraine handled by its own loss event.

1944: liberation of France (the former free zone). 'On 25 August 1944 Paris was liberated' and Operation Dragoon began 15 August (Liberation of France); the page's infobox runs the liberation '6 June 1944 - 8 May 1945', with the Atlantic pockets held to 8 May 1945 and Alsace-Lorraine handled by its own loss event.
1944: Monaco. German-occupied Europe table: '8 Sep 1943 - 3 Sep 1944'.

region.text: Eupen-Malmedy, the Belgian districts taken from Germany in 1919/1920, approximate

ledger.note: 1944: Eupen-Malmedy goes. 'In September 1944, American forces reached Eupen which became a centre of fierce fighting in the Battle of the Bulge' (Eupen); Eupen-Malmedy speaks of 'its first liberation in the fall of 1944' and 'returned to Belgium in 1945'. The German-occupied Europe table gives Belgium occupied to 4 February 1945 (ledger).

1944: Estonia retaken. The Baltic offensive ran '14 September - 24 November 1944'; the Tallinn offensive is dated '17-26 September 1944' and the Moonsund Landing '27 September-24 November 1944' (Baltic offensive). The month is the Tallinn offensive's; the islands were cleared in November.

1944: Lithuania retaken. Vilnius 'fell on 13 July' (Operation Bagration) and the Memel offensive is dated '5-22 October 1944' (Baltic offensive); the Lithuanian SSR dossier gives October 1944. The Memel district was Reich land and goes in January 1945.
1944: Albania. German-occupied Europe table: '8 Sep 1943 - 29 Nov 1944'.

1944: Alsace-Lorraine goes. 'Sudden Allied advances ... liberated Belfort, Mulhouse, and Strasbourg' in November, and 'American forces fought from September until mid-December' to push the Germans out of Lorraine (Liberation of France); the page dates neither Metz nor the end of the Colmar Pocket, which held part of Alsace into 1945. The counterpart is the state of the gain, as the Third Republic ended in 1940 and the Provisional Government has no dossier.
1945: Serbian Military Administration to January 1945; Yugoslavia occupied until 15 May 1945.

1945: the General Government ends. General Government infobox: 'USSR captures Warsaw: 17 January 1945', 'Disintegration: 19 January 1945' (Krakow, its capital, 19 January); the Vistula-Oder offensive page agrees (offensive began 12 January, Warsaw 17 January, Krakow 19 January).

region.text: eastern Germany: East Prussia, Pomerania, Silesia and Brandenburg east of the Oder

ledger.note: 1945: Soviet forces invade Germany, 13 January 1945 (German-occupied Europe timeline; Nazi Germany page: Soviet forces entered Germany on 27 January).

1945: the Memel district goes. Klaipeda was 'defended by the German Army during the Battle of Memel until 28 January 1945' and the Soviet Union 'incorporated the region into the Lithuanian SSR' (Klaipeda Region).

region.text: the Reichsgau Wartheland: Greater Poland and Lodz, approximate

ledger.note: 1945: Wartheland goes. 'The 8th Guards Army reached Lodz by 18 January, and took it by 19 January' and Poznan was encircled by 25 January with fighting in the city from the 26th (Vistula-Oder offensive); the page gives no capture date for Poznan, whose garrison held longer. The Reichsgau page gives only its creation (26 October 1939) and 'disestablishment 1 August 1945'. Counterpart: the Polish state (republic-of-poland, Cliopatria's only Polish row after 1939).

region.text: East Upper Silesia, the Katowice district, approximate

ledger.note: 1945: the Katowice district goes. 'German forces were allowed to withdraw from the Katowice salient on the night of 27 January, and Konev then secured the area undamaged' (Vistula-Oder offensive).

region.text: the Ciechanow (Zichenau) district, a radius, approximate

ledger.note: 1945: the Ciechanow district goes. The East Prussian offensive 'began on 13 January with a heavy preparatory bombardment' and the Vistula-Oder offensive on 12 January; neither page names Ciechanow or Zichenau, so the month is a bridge over a silence.
1945: Belgium occupied until 4 February 1945 (the table's end date).
1945: Luxembourg occupied until February 1945; the annexed Gau Moselland returns.
1945: Western Allied invasion of Germany, 22 March 1945 (timeline).

region.text: the former Free City of Danzig

ledger.note: 1945: Danzig goes. 'Danzig finally fell on 30 March 1945' (East Pomeranian offensive).

region.text: the Reichsgau Danzig-West Prussia: the Kuyavian-Pomeranian and Pomeranian voivodeships, approximate

ledger.note: 1945: Danzig-West Prussia goes. The East Pomeranian offensive ran '10 February - 4 April 1945'; 'Gdingen was taken on 26 March 1945' and Danzig on 30 March. The month is the offensive's close; the Vistula-Oder page does not date Bydgoszcz or Torun, so the southern part may have fallen in January or February.
1945: Denmark liberated: occupied until 5 May 1945.
1945: Norway occupied until 8 May 1945.
1945: Netherlands occupied until 20 May 1945 (the table's end date).
1945: the infobox gives 'Government dissolved: 8 May 1945' and 'Armed Forces surrender: 15 May 1945' (Independent State of Croatia); the client state ends with the Reich.
1945: Greece occupied until 8 May 1945.

1945: the occupation of the Czech lands ended in May 1945: the Prague uprising began 5 May, the Wehrmacht capitulated 8 May and 'Prague was taken on 9 May by Soviet troops'. Counterpart czechoslovakia, the state whose land was occupied.
1945: the Slovak Republic ends in May 1945 (table).

region.text: northern and central Italy outside the two Operational Zones

ledger.note: 1945: Italy, occupation to 2 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table).

region.text: the Operational Zones of the Adriatic Littoral and the Alpine Foothills

ledger.note: 1945: the zones end with the German surrender in Italy: the German and collaborationist troops of OZAK 'surrendered to the New Zealand 2nd Division on the evening of 2 May' (Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral); infobox 'Dissolution: 1945'. The page gives no exact dissolution date.
1945: Hungary occupied until May 1945.

region.text: Latvia, the last of the occupied Soviet land

ledger.note: 1945: Latvia. The Riga offensive ran '14 September-24 October 1944' and the Courland Pocket formed '15-22 October 1944'; the page gives 'the surrender of the Army Group Courland on 9 May 1945' (Baltic offensive), the last occupied Soviet land.
1945: Guernsey, occupied until 9 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table).
1945: Jersey, occupied until 9 May 1945 (German-occupied Europe table).
1945: Berlin surrendered on 2 May 1945 and the German Instrument of Surrender was signed on 8 May.
1945: the war in the west ends with the surrender of 8 May 1945.

region.text: the Sudetenland, the only land the Nazi Germany page names for the Munich settlement

ledger.note: 1945: the Sudetenland goes. 'In May 1945, Czechoslovak troops took possession of the borderland' (German occupation of Czechoslovakia); the page gives no day.

region.text: northern Slovenia: Lower Styria and the parts attached to Karnten, approximate

ledger.note: 1945: northern Slovenia goes. Lower Styria page: 'After World War II, Yugoslav authority over the region was established and Slovene Styria became an integral part of the Socialist Republic of Slovenia'; no date on the page (nor on Axis occupation of Yugoslavia), so the month is the end of the Reich.

region.text: the Reich within its 1937 borders, including the lands east of the Oder-Neisse line, plus Austria; the annexed lands have already gone through loss events

ledger.note: 1945: the Third Reich 'ended in May 1945, after 12 years': surrender 8 May 1945 (the Flensburg Government was arrested 23 May; the Berlin Declaration of 5/6 June assumed supreme authority; Potsdam 2 August moved the eastern border to the Oder-Neisse line).

wars.name: Invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: German victory: Poland occupied from 1 September 1939; decrees of 8 and 12 October 1939 annexed Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia and two districts.
wars.note: The Soviet share of Poland is the Soviet dossier's business.

wars.name: Norwegian campaign
wars.outcome: German victory: Denmark fell in under a day and Norway 'was fully occupied by early June'.

wars.name: Battle of France
wars.outcome: German victory: attack ordered for May 1940, occupation of the Low Countries from 10 May, France 'surrendered on 22 June'.

wars.name: Balkan campaign
wars.outcome: Germany invaded Yugoslavia and Greece on 6 April 1941; Yugoslavia occupied and partly annexed, Greece occupied.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War II)
wars.outcome: Invasion 22 June 1941; furthest advance 27 November 1941; Stalingrad surrender 31 January 1943; Kiev November 1943; the 1939 border regained 3 January 1944; Berlin surrendered 2 May 1945.
wars.note: Page silent on Bagration dates, the Courland pocket and the 1944 line.

wars.name: Allied invasion of Germany
wars.outcome: Soviet invasion of Germany 13 January 1945; Western Allied invasion 22 March 1945; Berlin surrendered 2 May; instrument of surrender 8 May 1945.

wars.name: German occupation of Italy
wars.outcome: Germany occupied Italian territory from 8 September 1943 to 2 May 1945 with the Italian Social Republic.

certainty.note: Treaty and decree lines (Saar plebiscite, Munich Agreement, Memel treaty of 23 March 1939, the October 1939 decrees); the General Government and the Protectorate boundaries are soft.
Fronts moved monthly and the pages opened give few lines; the annexed-land boundaries stay sharp.

notes: Cliopatria's Nazi Germany shapes draw the Reich plus occupied and allied Europe; this dossier corrects them to Reich-proper land and carries the rest as occupation_start/_end and vassal events (hatched/tinted). The state is founded in March 1933 at the Enabling Act (23 March), the month weimar-republic dissolves into it; 30 January 1933 is the seizure of power. Annexed lands are gained and lost with dated events: Sudetenland (October 1938 / May 1945), Memel (March 1939 / 28 January 1945), Danzig and the Polish districts (October 1939 / January-March 1945), Eupen-Malmedy (18 May 1940 / September 1944), Alsace-Lorraine (1940 / November 1944), Luxembourg (August 1942 / February 1945), the Bialystok district (1 August 1941 / July 1944), northern Slovenia (April 1941 / May 1945). The 1944 keyframe is the Reich at 1 January 1944, the 1945 keyframe the Reich at 1 January 1945. Region specs for annexed Polish land, Eupen-Malmedy, Alsace-Lorraine, the Operational Zones and the Ciechanow district are approximations (voivodeships, radii, modern provinces). Occupations are recorded against the state whose land was occupied: czechoslovakia (not the Protectorate), the Soviet republics one by one (RSFSR, Ukrainian, Byelorussian, Moldavian, Lithuanian, Latvian, Estonian), albania, principality-of-monaco, united-kingdom (Guernsey, Jersey), french-africa (Tunisia), kingdom-of-italy (Operational Zones and the north). The contests of 1941-1945 stay with the Union as a whole (union-of-soviet-socialist-republics has no dossier yet). Not settled: the Atlantic pockets and the Colmar Pocket (held into 1945; Liberation of France is silent on their dates); Poznan's capture date; the Ciechanow district's fall (pages silent, confidence 1); the date of Lower Styria's return (pages silent, confidence 1); Moldova (German occupation not shown by any page; the Moldavian SSR dossier records Romanian occupation); Denmark 1940-1945 (counterpart 'denmark' starts only in May 1945 while kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 dissolves into nazi-germany in April 1940: the Danish dossiers need one state for the occupation years); whether northern Italy is an occupation or a client of the Italian Social Republic (to settle with eu-21-x); Dalmatia (kingdom-of-italy counts it as lost to nazi-germany, but the Operational Zone page lists only Ljubljana of Italy's Yugoslav lands, so no German gain of Dalmatia is recorded). Counterparts needing dossiers: saar-basin-territory, protectorate-of-bohemia-and-moravia (now only a note), slovak-republic, italian-social-republic, republic-of-poland for 1945 (Cliopatria's row starts 1953), union-of-soviet-socialist-republics. Gazetteer names needed: Sudetenland, Wartheland, General Government, Eupen-Malmedy, Memel Territory (Memelland), Lower Styria, Ljubljana Province.
